[SUPERSEDED by the last note: the claim below holds only for a datetime.date value, which the repository never passes] the coercion_datatype site is Literal(betydningsbeskrivelse.modified, datatype=XSD.date): `modified` is typed `date` on Betydningsbeskrivelse (verified in the source repo's betydningsbeskrivelse.py), not a str, so INSTRUCTIONS.md's second pitfall applies -- a mechanical `{value}^^xsd:date` rewrite is unsafe for a non-string value. Checked on rdflib 7.2.1: Literal(datetime.date(2023,6,15), datatype=XSD.date) == Literal(datetime.date(2023,6,15)) (both lexical '2023-06-15', datatype xsd:date) -- rdflib's own default type inference for `datetime.date` already lands on xsd:date, so the language's default coercion (a bare `{expr}` in term position) reproduces the original's explicit datatype= exactly. Translated as bare interpolation, not `^^xsd:date`, per INSTRUCTIONS.md §2's 'la coercition du langage ... si la valeur n'est pas constante'
